title: Issue #180: catalog: define X35 deployment, release engineering and rollout governance contracts
content:
State: open

# X35 – Ecosystem Deployment, Release Engineering & Rollout Governance

**Architecture-ID:** `ATC-CROSSCUTTING-X35-DEPLOYMENT-RELEASE-ENGINEERING-ROLLOUT-GOVERNANCE`  
**Status:** `PROPOSED / NOT VERIFIED`  
**Scope:** 17 sublayers · 170 planned function contracts

## Goal and scope

Define cross-ecosystem contracts for build outputs, release candidates, deployment, staged rollouts, approvals, rollback/recovery, and evidence of the software version actually installed on a target.

Applies to:
- GlobusOS as a native installable OS, including kernel, system services, desktop and installer.
- A-TownChain blockchain/node releases and protocol compatibility.
- Canonical ATC-VM and ATCLang artifacts/toolchains.
- Aurora AI runtime, models, agents and adapters.
- Windows/Linux application operation only where platform support is actually evidenced.
- Ecosystem-level integration of approval status, provenance, compatibility and verification evidence.

X35 is a governance/integration layer, **not** another build engine, package manager, installer, updater or release pipeline.

## Boundaries

- **X10:** Supply Chain, Build Integrity & Artifact Provenance.
- **X15:** Update Management, Migration & Lifecycle Governance.
- **X23:** Product Lifecycle, Configuration Management & Portfolio Governance.
- **X35:** Controlled path from an approved build through rollout to verified target installation.

## Planned sublayers and contract IDs

All entries below are planned contracts, not assertions that functions already exist or are implemented.

| Sublayer | Planned contract IDs | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| X35.01 Release Identity & Version Governance | X35-001–X35-010 | Stable release identity, versioning, candidate/released state, source/build revision, platform and compatibility metadata, history and identity checks |
| X35.02 Build-to-Release Traceability | X35-011–X35-020 | Workflow/run/job/step evidence, full source SHA, exit codes, artifact hashes/formats, build configuration, provenance gaps and reproducibility |
| X35.03 Release Qualification & Readiness Gates | X35-021–X35-030 | Release-type criteria, mandatory checks, blocking failures, status separation, security/compatibility/migration checks, authorized exceptions and hash-bound decisions |
| X35.04 Release Approval & Separation of Duties | X35-031–X35-040 | Roles, separation of duties, hash-bound approvals, expiry/revocation, critical/emergency approval, conflicts, audit trail and deployment blocking |
| X35.05 Release Channels & Distribution Governance | X35-041–X35-050 | Development/preview/stable channels, channel transitions, protected unpublished artifacts, platform rules, revocation, mirrors, hash checks and distribution health |
| X35.06 Deployment Planning & Orchestration | X35-051–X35-060 | Targets, dependencies/order, preconditions, versioned plans, step state, conflict coordination, interruption handling, maintenance windows and partial success |
| X35.07 Progressive Rollouts & Exposure Control | X35-061–X35-070 | Rollout phases/scopes, observation windows, health gates, pause conditions, canaries, exposure policy, concurrent-change attribution and progress |
| X35.08 Installation, Provisioning & First Boot | X35-071–X35-080 | Platform profiles, image hashes, hardware/firmware prerequisites, provisioning, applicable Secure Boot/signature checks, first identity, retries and installed-version evidence |
| X35.09 Operating System & Kernel Deployment | X35-081–X35-090 | Separate OS/kernel artifacts, bootloader/services dependencies, platform checks, bootable states, policy gates, startup diagnostics, recovery, drivers and rollback limits |
| X35.10 Blockchain Node & Protocol Release Coordination | X35-091–X35-100 | Node/protocol versioning, network/chain compatibility, activation, migration, incompatible versions, rollout order, validator risk, chain-state checks and evidence for protocol approvals |
| X35.11 Application, VM & Language Runtime Releases | X35-101–X35-110 | Application/runtime catalog, canonical VM binding, bytecode/format compatibility, ATCLang toolchain, language conformance, compiler/runtime dependencies and compatibility tests |
| X35.12 Aurora AI Model, Agent & Runtime Releases | X35-111–X35-120 | Runtime/agent/model provenance, capability/tool compatibility, sandbox checks, local/external backend support, rollout metrics, approval-path integrity, rollback and privacy/residency |
| X35.13 Configuration, Secrets & Environment Promotion | X35-121–X35-130 | Versioned environment profiles, build/runtime separation, secret references, schema validation, promotion, privilege/secret controls, drift and effective configuration evidence |
| X35.14 Database, State & Migration Release Governance | X35-131–X35-140 | Versioned migrations, pre/postconditions, data compatibility, backups, idempotency, checkpoints, partial migration recovery, irreversible boundaries and integrity invariants |
| X35.15 Rollback, Rollforward & Release Recovery | X35-141–X35-150 | Recovery prerequisites/artifacts, explicit triggers, rollforward for irreversible changes, state assessment, retry safety, escalation, completion criteria and active-version verification |
| X35.16 Post-Deployment Verification & Release Health | X35-151–X35-160 | Installed-manifest match, health checks, smoke tests, invariants, telemetry quality, regression, error/latency gates, conflicting/missing evidence and target/run references |
| X35.17 Release Audit, Compliance & Lifecycle Closure | X35-161–X35-170 | Evidence packages, SHA/hash/approval linkage, run/job/step and exit codes, exceptions, retention/access, revocation, vulnerability/dependency state, catalog reconciliation and lifecycle closure |

## Proposed data contract: `ATC-RELEASE-CONTRACT-V1`

This YAML is a design proposal only; it is **not** normative until formally reviewed and registered in `atc-standards`.

```yaml
contract_id: ATC-RELEASE-CONTRACT-V1
schema_version: 1

release:
  release_id: required
  component_id: required
  version: required
  release_channel: required
  target_platforms: required
  release_status: required

source:
  repository: required
  commit_sha: required
  source_tree_sha: conditional

build:
  workflow_run_ref: required
  job_and_step_evidence: required
  exit_codes: required
  artifact_manifest_ref: required
  artifact_hashes: required

qualification:
  required_checks: required
  compatibility_report_ref: required
  security_review_ref: conditional
  approval_refs: required

rollout:
  deployment_plan_ref: required
  target_scope: required
  rollout_strategy: required
  health_gate_ref: required
  rollback_or_recovery_plan_ref: required

verification:
  installed_version_evidence: conditional
  post_deployment_test_ref: conditional
  final_status: required

rules:
  missing_provenance: blocked
  failed_required_check: blocked
  artifact_hash_mismatch: reject
  unknown_compatibility: unresolved
  unverified_deployment: not_verified
```

Before normative adoption, define field types, hash algorithms, error codes, signature/approval semantics, and platform-specific mandatory fields.

## Canonical SSOT boundaries

- `a-townchain-ecosystem`: release architecture, catalog, integration/compliance/evidence and drift reconciliation only.
- `atc-standards`: normative release/artifact contracts only after formal registration.
- `a-townchain`: blockchain core and node/protocol releases.
- `a-townchain/components/vm`: canonical ATC-VM.
- `a-townchain/components/algorithm`: canonical algorithm/consensus implementation.
- `globus-os/modules/atc-shivacore/kernel/`: canonical kernel and kernel-near components.
- `globus-os`: OS, installer, system services and platform integration according to actual module structure.
- Aurora AI/runtime: canonical repository and paths must be verified before mapping.
- ATCLang/toolchain: canonical implementation and paths must be verified before release mapping.
- CI/build/distribution: each component's canonical repository workflows and release configuration.

The ecosystem may aggregate release metadata and verification evidence; it must not create duplicate implementations, an alternate installer, or a parallel release pipeline in place of canonical components.

## Mandatory invariants

1. Approval and deployment bind to exact artifact hashes and full source commits, not version labels alone.
2. Missing mandatory evidence or failed required checks blocks release/deployment.
3. A successful build does not prove installability or production readiness.
4. No blind rollback: data migrations, irreversible state changes and blockchain protocol changes require specific recovery rules.
5. Canonical implementations remain authoritative; do not duplicate installers, updaters, compilers or runtimes in the ecosystem repository.
6. Platform support is claimed only where appropriate artifacts and tests are evidenced.
7. Approvals can be revoked; emergency exceptions are scoped, attributable and subject to review.
8. Rollout expansion requires predeclared, evidenced health gates.
9. Release approval and successful installation are distinct states.
10. `VERIFIED` requires inspectable evidence. Missing/incomplete evidence remains `NOT VERIFIED`, `BLOCKED` or `UNRESOLVED`.
11. `demo-repository` is excluded from the live drift gate.
12. Green CI alone is not verification.

## Implementation sequence

1. Inventory existing release workflows, artifacts, installers, updaters and distribution channels; map exact SSOT paths.
2. Specify the manifest, release identity, required checks, approval roles and compatibility criteria.
3. Map deployment plans, target groups, staged rollout, health gates and stop criteria to existing canonical implementations.
4. Integrate GlobusOS installation, blockchain node releases, ATC-VM, ATCLang and Aurora runtime using their canonical release processes.
5. Test rollback/rollforward, migration failures, interrupted installation and invalid artifacts.
6. Archive full commit SHAs, run/job/step results, exit codes, logs and artifact hashes before changing verification status.

## Readiness checklist (initially 0/12)

- [ ] Inventory current release/deployment processes.
- [ ] Record canonical repositories and workflow paths.
- [ ] Compare all 170 planned contracts with the existing catalog.
- [ ] Specify release manifest and version rules.
- [ ] Define mandatory checks and approval gates.
- [ ] Test artifact provenance and hash verification.
- [ ] Evidence installer and platform compatibility.
- [ ] Test staged rollout and health gates.
- [ ] Verify rollback and recovery paths.
- [ ] Assess blockchain and data migrations separately.
- [ ] Demonstrate post-deployment verification.
- [ ] Archive complete release evidence and exact SHAs.

This checklist is tracking metadata only; it does not itself verify repository state or CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each planned contract is classified against catalog evidence as `MAPPED`, `MISSING`, `UNRESOLVED` or `EXCLUDED` with a reason.
- Every mapped implementation cites exact repository, full commit SHA, path, symbol/blob and supporting evidence.
- Missing contracts are added to the catalog without duplicating canonical implementation.
- Release manifests and readiness/approval gates are explicitly marked proposed until the standard is registered.
- Deployment and installed-version verification are demonstrated separately from build success.
- Full evidence includes run → job → step, exit codes/logs and artifact hashes.
- Status is not promoted to `VERIFIED` based solely on green CI.

## Current status

- Architecture: `PROPOSED`
- Catalog intake: `NOT VERIFIED`
- Implementation: `UNRESOLVED`
- Planned sublayers: 17
- Planned function contracts: 170

**Next required step:** reconcile X35 with the existing catalog, map existing release functions to their canonical sources, and add only genuinely missing contracts. Until repository and CI evidence is reviewed, retain `PROPOSED / NOT VERIFIED`.
